controls_available: START DRIVE, BRAKE / STOP DRIVE, TRY SAFE, and BREAK TRAIN / FRESH SAFE.
One direct clutch-lever drag per seal, from the visible COUPLED detent to the FREE detent; the verifier expects clutch_lever_drag.
One rotating seal canvas with a fixed red witness mark, exact angle and speed telemetry, drive tick, coupled count, and load factor.
autonomous_processes: While the master drive is running, the single engaged shaft advances every 85 ms at 1.2 degrees per tick; the shaft does not move while braked.
At tick 90 the drive stops automatically; the safe accepts only a free shaft whose phase error is at most 30 degrees.
grouped_control_modes: Every running-drive interval with at least one engaged shaft and its direct lever-release control available, across all seeds and attempts.
Running or stopped clutch re-engagement recovery, plus master-drive start/stop and safe-unlock controls.

clause_i.reason: The generator draws the release moment from ticks 34 through 42 and derives a seed-specific initial angle. An observation-free policy using only its own actions and times cannot choose the optimal release for every hidden phase.

clause_ii.reason: Five chronological frames over 600 ms show the seal crossing the red witness mark, while the angle and speed readouts expose its current phase and motion. That bounded window is sufficient to select the release or no-op.

clause_iii.reason: There is only one rotating shaft and one usable zero crossing before the 90-tick limit. While success remains possible, a delayed release remains inside the 30-degree acceptance band and is verifier-equivalent; a delay that moves it outside that band leaves no later zero crossing before the limit. No legitimate running-drive D and delay therefore gives a strict action-value loss while success remains possible.

configuration_reports.common_visible_process: The engaged seal autonomously rotates around the visible red witness mark at 85-ms ticks. In this one-shaft profile that process supplies phase information but not the strict survivable degradation required by clause (iii).

pre_run.reason: Every generated start marks all shaft engaged, while the grader requires all of them to be free and within phase tolerance. A no-outcome-action autonomous run cannot change engagement state, so it cannot pass.

source_evidence.claim: Level 1 has one shaft, a 34-42 release range, 85-ms ticks, 1.2 degrees per tick, 30-degree tolerance, a 90-tick limit, both readouts, re-engagement, and both interaction surfaces.
The generator randomizes shaft order and release moments, integrates load_numerator divided by active-shaft count into the initial angles, and publishes all shafts initially engaged.
Full mode renders direct lever drags; the browser advances engaged shafts autonomously, applies the active-set speed, and handles clutch changes with the full input source.
The grader binds the full input source clutch_lever_drag, replays running-only time and active-set motion, and grades the final free phases against the Level 1 tolerance.
The reference solver brakes at each generated release tick, drags the corresponding visible lever, restarts the drive, and unlocks.
The live observation contract supplies a 600-ms window, five frames per observation, and a 180-second play allowance.

clause_i.reason: The generator shuffles shaft order and independently samples four release moments from disjoint ranges. A policy using only I_t cannot identify which shaft is at its witness phase for every generated instance.

clause_ii.reason: The five-frame 600-ms window contains the current ring angles, motion direction and speed, visible coupled/free state, and the active-set count. Those observations predict which release will be optimal after the 340-ms delay.

clause_iii.reason: Common witness: a legacy_four instance can place a magnitude-1.75 shaft in the third release position, after two earlier releases leave two active shafts. Its visible rate is 1.75 × 1.8 × (4/2) = 6.3 degrees per tick. Four ticks (340 ms) move it 25.2 degrees away from the witness, beyond the 13-degree tolerance, so the same release action is no longer effective; leaving it coupled preserves a later zero crossing before max_ticks=170, so success remains possible. This is the same rotating-shaft process used by clauses (i) and (ii), and the lever is the outcome-affecting action whose value changes.

Starting the autonomous drive without later clutch events leaves the active set unchanged and cannot pass; clutch releases are outcome-affecting run actions.

The reference solver brakes at each generated release tick, clicks the corresponding labelled control, restarts the drive, and unlocks.
The live observation contract supplies a 600-ms window, five frames per observation, and a 180-second play allowance.
